correctness.rationale: Arbitrary antiderivative tests in \(x\) and \(y\) give the two conditional expectations. The inspected package's critical polynomial certificate \(F=z+xy+x\) satisfies exactly \(LF=a-x^2+4y^2\), hence stationarity yields the RMS identity. For \(a>0\), equality forces \(y=0\) on invariant support, then successively \(z=0\) and \(x^2=a\), so the support lies on the two equilibria; any other invariant measure has positive \(y^2\), hence \(x^2\)-mean strictly above \(a\), forcing mass outside \(|x|\le\sqrt a\). Its zero mean and nonzero second moment also force both signs of \(y\). For \(a<0\), nonnegativity gives \(\mathbb E[y^2]\ge-a/4\); equality would force \(x=0\) on invariant support and then \(y=z=0\), contradicting \(\dot z=a\ne0\), so the floor is strict.

value.rationale: The Chen--Wang model was designed around a transition in the number of equilibria. The exact RMS law shows that the same transition has a sharp statistical counterpart for every compact recurrent state: equilibrium mixtures are the unique equality states on the positive side and a strict kinetic floor survives on the no-equilibrium side. This is a natural global invariant tied directly to the model's motivating parameter transition.

final_claim: For the plus-sign Chen--Wang flow \(\dot x=y\), \(\dot y=z\), \(\dot z=-y-x^2-xz+3y^2+a\), every compactly supported invariant probability measure satisfies \(\mathbb E[y\mid x]=0\), \(\mathbb E[z\mid y]=0\), and \(\mathbb E[x^2]=a+4\mathbb E[y^2]\); for \(a>0\) equality \(\mathbb E[x^2]=a\) occurs exactly for mixtures of the two equilibrium atoms and every other compact recurrent state exits the equilibrium-amplitude slab, while for \(a<0\) every compact recurrent state, if one exists, has the strict floor \(\mathbb E[y^2]>-a/4\).
limitations: The theorem uses the plus-sign normalization fixed in the later rigorous Chen--Wang literature.
For \(a<0\), the RMS floor is conditional on existence of compact recurrence and does not prove an attractor exists.
